title: Is the cheap TV box worth it?
source: Matt's brief; Canadian prices checked October 2026 via news and provider sites; legal context from the 2019 GoldTV Federal Court order. Not legal advice.

beats.say: Will the cheap TV box just work, the way Telus TV does? ... Short answer, not quite. ... It saves real money, but it comes with catches.

Before, TV cost about two thousand dollars a year. ... Telus was nine hundred, Sportsnet plus alone is three fifty, and the other subscriptions are roughly seven fifty. ... With Telus gone, that's about eleven hundred.

Here are four ways forward, in yearly costs. ... Keep everything as is, about eleven hundred. ... The box service plus the other subscriptions, around a thousand. ... The box service alone, one fifty to four hundred. ... Or trim and use Plex, about six hundred and twenty. ... The box itself is a one-time purchase on top, roughly fifty to a hundred dollars.

The appeal is easy to see. ... It's cheaper than cable, with a huge number of channels. ... Setup is simple, and trials or monthly plans cap the risk. ... A coworker vouches for it, though that's one person.

But it isn't Telus. ... This is a reseller of streams the channels never licensed, so it can vanish mid-term with no refund. ... Expect buffering at peak times like hockey night, possible blocking by your internet company, and no way to dispute an e-transfer.

Tech support lands on you. ... Help is one person on WhatsApp. ... Apps are side-loaded, there are no profiles, and fifteen thousand channels are hard to dig through. ... Expect a few calls a month, and some outages.
Plex is the free option worth knowing. ... Hundreds of live channels, tens of thousands of free movies and shows, with ads, plus some Canadian channels. ... It runs on most TVs, but there's no NHL.

So, trim first. ... Add Plex, pay for hockey only in season, and drop overlapping subscriptions. ... That gets close to six hundred twenty a year. ... If the box is still tempting, pay month to month, and keep another way to watch hockey in case it stops working.
